tips.title: Submit the SG Arrival Card
tips.body: Every traveller clearing immigration must submit the SG Arrival Card with its electronic health declaration within three days before arrival, counting the arrival day. It is free on the ICA website or the MyICA app. Passengers transiting without clearing immigration are exempt.

tips.title: Avoid paid arrival-card websites
tips.body: ICA does not endorse commercial websites that charge to submit the SG Arrival Card for you. Use only the official ICA site or the MyICA app.

tips.title: Vapes are illegal
tips.body: Vapes have been banned since 2018, and from 1 September 2025 enforcement got tougher: devices are seized and users are fined. Short-term visitors who reoffend can be banned from entering Singapore again.

tips.title: Etomidate 'Kpods' count as a drug
tips.body: Etomidate is now a Class C drug, with penalties of up to 10 years' jail and a S$20,000 fine for possession or use. Foreigners caught with it, or who test positive, can be deported and banned.

tips.title: No chewing gum imports
tips.body: Importing, buying or selling chewing gum is banned, so leave it at home. The law does not cover chewing it.

tips.title: Littering fines are real
tips.body: First-time litterers can be fined up to S$300, even for a tissue. Use the bins.

tips.title: No eating or drinking on the MRT
tips.body: Eating and drinking, including water, is banned on trains, with fines up to S$500. Stand on the left of escalators.

tips.title: Alcohol sales stop at 10:30pm
tips.body: Under the Liquor Control Act, shops such as 7-Eleven cannot sell alcohol after 10:30pm. Plan ahead if you want a drink later.

tips.title: Tap your own card on MRT and buses
tips.body: Foreign contactless Visa and Mastercard cards and mobile wallets work at fare gates with no registration (SimplyGo). Admin fees apply to foreign-issued cards.

tips.title: EZ-Link card or Tourist Pass
tips.body: An adult EZ-Link or NETS FlashPay card costs S$10, including S$5 of stored value, at stations and convenience stores. The Singapore Tourist Pass gives unlimited rides for 1–3 days and is sold at SimplyGo Ticket Offices.

tips.title: Exact change on buses
tips.body: Buses accept cash, but no change is given, so pay the exact fare or tap a card instead.

tips.title: Travel eSIMs need no registration
tips.body: Travel eSIMs on Singtel, M1 or StarHub need no passport registration, and coverage is strong across the island, including MRT tunnels and Sentosa.
